- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently fallen.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — especially after a spike — leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., reduce forecast by 5–10% after a +20%+ spike).
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model often misaligns with true trend; favor smoother, trend-following adjustments over sentiment-driven extremes.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid sharp downward revisions unless sentiment is clearly bearish (e.g., 3 consecutive -1.00); otherwise, allow gradual decay from recent highs.
